_comment: NFR-15 (latency) + NFR-16 (throughput) — pinned pilot-site bench budgets. Every entry is a MAXIMUM for the latency/error dimensions and a MINIMUM for throughput. Per-concurrency overrides, when present, take precedence over the global ceiling.

_pins.referenceHardware: Ubuntu Server 24.04 LTS · 4 vCPU · 4 GiB RAM · 64 GiB SSD
_pins.updatePolicy: Changing any limit requires an ADR + a dated evidence run under docs/evaluation/evidence/ showing the new limit is tight enough. Per-concurrency overrides are REQUIRED when the global ceiling doesn't fit — don't loosen the global without documenting why.

latencyMs._note: Applies to every concurrency level unless overridden under perConcurrency. Aligns with NFR-18 resource-budget p95 ceiling.

throughputRps._note: Sustained successful requests/second. Minimum MUST be met at every concurrency level — falling below is a saturation failure.

errors._note: No benign error rate at the pilot hardware target. Any failure is a regression — a slight allowance leaves room for transient DNS or socket exhaustion under the 20-user peak.
